plan.risks: Subtractive by design for non-backend-capable sites (a site without 'backend' in deploy_config.capabilities will stop being offered intent-probe by content-gap-planner and build-site-planner) — this is the intended effect, verified to remove exactly and only intent-probe via the disagreeing-pair proof, nothing else. Nil-param outage risk on 418 is mitigated by the 131/131 binding proof against live orchestration history; 419 reuses migration 407's already-proven binding, unchanged. 420 deliberately avoids this risk by using no binding at all. Concurrent-edit risk on the content-gap-planner row (already edited twice by an unrelated session, migrations 413/414, in the hours around authoring) is mitigated by id-scoped UPDATEs with byte-exact pre-state gates that abort the whole transaction on any mismatch rather than silently double-applying or clobbering a concurrent change; all three migrations were dry-run (COMMIT swapped for ROLLBACK) with both DO blocks passing, and the pre-state gate was mutation-tested against a deliberately wrong literal to confirm it can actually fail. site-planner (420) is unexercisable today (zero dispatches ever), so its fix cannot be verified against a live run — only against the direct-SQL disagreeing-pair proof. No architecture RFC filed: two live owner rulings (2026-08-02 §1 and §2) already cover an opt-in tag with the unsafe side defaulting OFF and the producer/consumer set named in the register entry, exactly as already established for the tool-side gate (406).
